summary: Iter 17 — BotNira Phase 2 Google Calendar/Meet integration verified end-to-end (up to Google OAuth handoff, per instructions — Google login itself NOT automated). Backend pytest 6/6 pass against deployed preview URL as vendor kamal@thedigisparrow.com: (1) GET /api/scheduling/google/status → 200 {configured:true, connected:false}; (2) GET /api/scheduling/google/connect?origin=https://x.com → 200 with authorization_url that starts with https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth AND contains client_id=201113663178-ddtt37kt350bqms5q1t7he6fi4vvmb8h.apps.googleusercontent.com AND redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fx.com%2Fapi%2Foauth%2Fcalendar%2Fcallback AND response_type=code AND access_type=offline AND prompt=consent AND a signed state JWT; (3) unauthenticated /connect → 401/403; (4) GET /api/oauth/calendar/callback?state=bogus&code=x → HTTP 400 'Invalid or expired state'; (5) POST /api/scheduling/google/disconnect → 200 {ok:true} idempotent; (6) status after disconnect → connected:false. Frontend Playwright: logged in via password form (Sign in button — not type=submit) → /app/appointments → clicked appt-tab-calendars → CalendarsTab renders (data-testid calendars-tab) → gcal-status-disconnected chip visible, gcal-connect-btn visible, ZERO 'Setup required' amber boxes on the page (confirming GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID+SECRET are picked up by the backend). Clicking gcal-connect-btn triggered a REAL browser navigation toward https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth?client_id=201113663178-...&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fmulti-channel-inbox-3.preview.emergentagent.com%2Fapi%2Foauth%2Fcalendar%2Fcallback&response_type=code&scope=…calendar…&access_type=offline&prompt=consent&state=<JWT> — captured via page.route interceptor which aborted the request before the Google page loaded (per instructions to NOT try to complete Google's OAuth). Mobile 390x844: no horizontal page overflow (scrollWidth==clientWidth==390), Connect button rendered at (x=40, y=400, w=272, h=52) — fully tappable.
critical_code_review_comments: google_calendar_routes.py:_get_creds catches refresh failure and returns None but still leaves stale access_token in DB — fine because push/pull all re-call _get_creds, but consider clearing access_token on error so a partial disconnect doesn't try to use a dead token. Non-blocking.

The connect endpoint accepts an arbitrary origin= from the client and echoes it into redirect_uri. That's fine because Google only accepts redirect_uris pre-registered on the Cloud Console OAuth client, so a spoofed origin will just fail at Google's end. Still worth documenting: only origins added to the Google Cloud Console's Authorized redirect URIs will work in production — deployers must add the preview URL AND the production URL there. Not a bug, just a deploy-time note for the main agent.
CalendarsTab.jsx uses window.location.href = data.authorization_url which is correct (avoids CORS on the cross-origin Google URL). Verified in Playwright — behaves as intended.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (Calendars tab render, status chip, no Setup-required box, Connect redirect target params, mobile no-overflow, mobile button tappable — all pass)

test_credentials: Vendor kamal@thedigisparrow.com / Kamala98@hmu (exempt account). No new users created; disconnect was called at the end of the pytest run to leave vendor in a clean (not-connected) state.
seed_data_creation: None. Any pre-existing gcal_connections row for the vendor was cleared by test_disconnect_returns_ok at end of run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Phase 2 Google Calendar wiring works up to and including the redirect to accounts.google.com. Google's actual consent screen CANNOT be automated (Google bot-blocks headless browsers) — the human user must complete it manually. To re-verify the redirect target in Playwright: (a) after login+navigate to /app/appointments+click Calendars tab, install a page.route('**/*', handler) that awaits route.abort() when 'accounts.google.com' is in request.url — the request URL is captured BEFORE the navigation lands, avoiding 'chrome-error://' issues. (b) The backend authorization_url includes a JWT state signed with server.JWT_SECRET containing {vendor_id, origin, exp}. (c) The public callback /api/oauth/calendar/callback is mounted under /api and NOT vendor-authenticated (Google calls it directly). Bogus state → 400 with detail 'Invalid or expired state'. (d) Google creds in backend/.env: GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=201113663178-…apps.googleusercontent.com, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=GOCSPX-…. If Google login shows 'redirect_uri_mismatch' during manual test, the deployer needs to add the current preview URL's /api/oauth/calendar/callback to the OAuth client's Authorized redirect URIs in Google Cloud Console.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found. Everything requested by the review works correctly.
